about: The evangelium of the formulary “24th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: When you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place — let the reader understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let him who is on the roof not come down to take anything out of his house; and let him who is in the field not return to take his tunic. But woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days. And pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the sabbath. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor will be. And if those days had not been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened. Then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is the Christ, or there, do not believe it. For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will work great signs and wonders, so that even the elect, if possible, would be led into error. Behold, I have foretold it to you. So if they say to you: Behold, He is in the desert, do not go out; Behold, in the inner rooms, do not believe it. For as the lightning comes forth from the east and is seen as far as the west, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be. Wherever the body is, there the eagles also will be gathered together. And immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken; and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. And He will send His angels with a trumpet and a loud voice, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens to their limits. Now learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branch is already tender and the leaves have come out, you know that summer is near. So you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors. Amen I say to you that this generation will not pass away until all these things come to pass. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
